assignment_html:
Scenario

Purpose: Translate a specified Bug2 detour into distance calculations without using the full rectangle perimeter.

A robot starts at O = (0, 0) and travels east toward G = (10, 0) along the Bug2 m-line. A rectangular obstacle has corners A = (4, -1), B = (6, -1), C = (6, 1), and D = (4, 1).

  • Hit point: H = (4, 0).
  • Leave point: L = (6, 0).
  • Required right-turn route: O -> H -> A -> B -> L -> G.

L is on the m-line and is closer to G than H, so the robot leaves the boundary at L.

Task

  1. Set distance_to_obstacle to the Euclidean distance from O to H.
  2. Set distance_along_obstacle to H-to-A plus A-to-B plus B-to-L.
  3. Set distance_from_obstacle_to_goal to the Euclidean distance from L to G.
  4. Set total_path_length to the sum of those three traveled components exactly once.

distance = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2)

Hints

Rules and required outputs

  • Follow exactly H -> A -> B -> L. Do not use C, D, the upper boundary, or the full perimeter.
  • Treat the robot as a point and ignore its width and turning radius.
  • Required numeric variables: distance_to_obstacle, distance_along_obstacle, distance_from_obstacle_to_goal, and total_path_length.

Before you run the tests

  • Confirm that the boundary distance contains exactly three segments.
  • Confirm that total_path_length contains the approach, boundary, and departure components once each.
learning_objectives: Locate Bug2 hit and leave points where a rectangular obstacle intersects the m-line.
Translate a specified right-turn boundary route into Euclidean line segments.
Distinguish the traveled boundary distance from the full obstacle perimeter.
Compose a complete path length without omitting or double-counting segments.

rubric.description: Calculate the distance from O to the actual obstacle hit point.
Add only the H-to-A, A-to-B, and B-to-L boundary segments.
Calculate the straight distance from the leave point to G.
Add the three traveled components exactly once.

common_misconceptions.description: Uses a rectangle corner instead of the specified hit point H.
Uses the full perimeter or a different boundary direction instead of H-to-A-to-B-to-L.
Starts the final segment at a corner instead of leave point L.
Omits or double-counts a traveled route component.

tutoring_rules.tone: Socratic, encouraging, and precise about route endpoints

solution_html:
1. Approach

The m-line distance from O(0,0) to H(4,0) is 4 units.

2. Boundary detour

The route H to A to B to L has lengths 1, 2, and 1, totaling 4 units.

3. Continue to the goal

The m-line distance from L(6,0) to G(10,0) is 4 units.

Total path: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 units.
